methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines a large GPS-based peptidomic screen of disease-relevant nonstop mutations with full-length validation, CHX-chase experiments, sequence analysis, random peptide libraries, and CRISPR/Cas9 screens for C-terminal degradation machinery. It directly improves on prior GFP-only comparator logic by comparing readthrough C-termini with the corresponding wild-type C-termini. Statistical methods include replicate correlation, unpaired two-tailed t tests, permutation tests, and p-value thresholds, but there is no power calculation and several mechanistic validations rely on standard small-n laboratory assays.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is preclinical and largely cell-line, reporter, and computational sequence analysis, so it maps to Oxford level 5. It has oncology relevance because it functionally annotates nonstop mutations in oncoproteins and tumor suppressors, including examples such as CCND2, FOXA1, PTEN, CTCF, and BCL2L11. The manuscript does not connect the variants to patient outcomes or therapeutic response, so clinical relevance remains translational rather than demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: No listed clinical checklist cleanly applies, so 'other' is most appropriate for this functional genomics and cell-biology study. The manuscript reports screen design, biological replicate structure, PSI calculation, CRISPR screen approach, statistical analyses, and a Nature Portfolio reporting summary. Source data and supplementary data are referenced, but the normalized text does not show a complete raw sequencing repository or analysis-code availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: The study makes a meaningful conceptual and empirical advance by showing that disease-associated nonstop C-terminal extensions can stabilize as well as destabilize proteins when compared with matched wild-type C-termini. It also identifies Cys/Trp enrichment and additional E3 ligases, RNF139 and MARCH6, as contributors to degradation of hydrophobic C-termini. Prior C-degron and readthrough quality-control work is well positioned, so this is a strong extension rather than a first description of the pathway.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized around nonstop mutations, physiological C-terminal variation, sequence determinants, and ubiquitin ligase mechanisms. The abstract is self-contained and accurately conveys the major conclusion that erroneous C-termini can stabilize or destabilize proteins. Captions provide enough information about screen design, replicate structure, and validation assays, although the breadth of screens and sequence analyses makes the presentation dense.

key_strengths: Large-scale functional screen directly compares disease-relevant readthrough C-termini with matched wild-type C-termini.
Multiple orthogonal validations include full-length constructs, CHX chase, random peptide assays, and CRISPR screens.
The study revises a prior one-direction model of nonstop mutation effects by showing both stabilizing and destabilizing outcomes.
key_concerns: Clinical impact is inferred from variant annotation and cancer-gene status rather than patient outcome data.
The work remains mostly reporter and cell-line based, so endogenous disease-context effects may differ.
Raw data and code availability are not fully visible in the normalized manuscript beyond source and supplementary data references.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong, broad functional genomics paper with clear mechanistic novelty and oncology relevance. Tier 2 with minor revisions is appropriate because the findings are robust but not yet clinically validated.
